Enterprise and hyperscale adoption of NVIDIA Hopper (H100/H200) and Blackwell (B200/GB200) architectures continues to expand across four distinct customer segments: Hyperscale Cloud Service Providers (Tier-1 CSPs), Emerging GPU Cloud Specialists (Tier-2 Neoclouds), Sovereign AI Programs, and Fortune 500 Enterprise On-Premises deployments.

AMD offers the Instinct MI300 Series of data center AI accelerators, including the MI300X, MI300A, and MI325X, built on CDNA 3 architecture for AI and HPC workloads. The MI325X provides 256 GB of HBM3E memory, 6 TB/s peak memory bandwidth, and 304 compute units for training and inference. These accelerators support precision formats from INT8 and FP8 to FP64 for HPC.

AMD targets data center, edge, and end-user customer segments with AI solutions deployable on-premises and in the cloud. The company offers CPU, GPU, and adaptable computing solutions for optimized deployments tailored to customer needs. AMD's technologies advance the future of the data center, embedded, gaming, and PC markets.

AMD Instinct MI300 accelerators are adopted by cloud providers such as Microsoft Azure and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, OEMs including Dell, HPE, Lenovo, and Supermicro, and government/HPC customers such as Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory's El Capitan supercomputer. Specialized AI cloud providers including Aligned, Arkon Energy, Cirrascale, Crusoe, Denvr Dataworks, and Tensorwave also plan to offer MI300X access. Dell announced integration of MI300X with PowerEdge XE9680 servers for generative AI workloads.

AMD: By the mid-2020s, AMD had become a major player in data center and AI computing. Its Instinct line of accelerators has been adopted by major cloud providers and research organizations for running large AI models. In October 2025, AMD signed a chip-supply agreement with OpenAI and a $1 billion agreement with the U.S. Department of Energy for federal high-performance computing chips.

AMD: ROCm is an open software stack that includes programming models, tools, compilers, libraries, and runtimes for AI and HPC solution development on AMD GPUs. Developers can use PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX with AMD-optimized containers and workflows, and use HIP to adapt existing GPU applications and frameworks for supported AMD hardware. The stack helps data center teams quickly set up, deploy, and scale AI and HPC workloads across GPUs and nodes.

AMD: ROCm supports AI training at scale through AMD Primus and ROCm communication libraries for pre-training, fine-tuning, and distributed training across AMD Instinct GPUs. For inference, ROCm provides AMD Quark, AITER, vLLM, and SGLang to optimize models and deploy high-throughput serving from individual GPUs to multi-node environments using containers, Kubernetes, Slurm, and telemetry. ROCm also provides a CLI for unified setup, management, and operation of AI workloads on AMD hardware.

AMD: ROCm 7.0 supports PyTorch 2.7 and 2.8, TensorFlow 2.19.1, and JAX 0.6.x with day-0 framework support, and enables hardware for the Instinct MI350X and MI355X with FP4, FP6, and FP8 precision formats. The release also includes AITER pre-optimized operators and production-ready models from AMD Quark. Developers can run leading frameworks with ROCm 7.0 while taking advantage of performance optimizations and tighter integrations across the stack.

AMD: ROCm officially supports AMD Instinct accelerators including MI355X, MI350X, MI325X, MI300X, MI300A, MI250X, MI250, MI210, and MI100, as well as select Radeon, Radeon PRO, and Radeon AI PRO graphics cards for compute workloads. Unsupported or deprecated GPUs are explicitly excluded from official ROCm support. Support status varies by GPU architecture and LLVM target.

AMD: ROCm includes AI-driven development capabilities such as AMD Skills, which allow agentic coding tools like Cursor, Claude, Codex, and Gemini to understand ROCm natively. The stack also includes Hyperloom for AI-assisted workload optimization and the ROCm Core SDK as the foundational software stack. These tools are designed to accelerate development velocity and performance optimization on AMD GPUs.

AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs are available through cloud providers including Microsoft Azure via the ND MI300x v5 virtual machine series, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure via MI300X-based bare metal instances and OCI Supercluster, and specialized AI cloud providers such as TensorWave, Aligned, Arkon Energy, Cirrascale, Crusoe, and Denvr Dataworks. Oracle plans to support OCI Supercluster with ultrafast RDMA networking. These cloud offerings target AI workloads and high-performance accelerated computing instances.

AMD: The AMD Developer Cloud provides access to AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs through a third-party cloud website, Digital Ocean. AMD AI Developer Program members receive complimentary $100 credits, and pay-as-you-go options are available for scaling AI workloads. Pre-installed Docker containers and Jupyter Notebook environments minimize setup time for developers.

AMD: TensorWave offers AMD Instinct MI300X GPUs available now and is seeing increased demand for the product. Lamini uses MI300X and MI210 at scale to help companies build enterprise LLM offerings. Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Dell, Supermicro, and Lenovo are bringing MI300X-powered systems to market.

AMD offers the Instinct MI300 Series data center GPU based on the CDNA 3 architecture for HPC, AI, and machine learning workloads. The MI300 Series uses an Accelerator Complex Die (XCD) design with up to 8 vertically stacked XCDs, 8 stacks of HBM3, and 4 I/O dies linked by AMD Infinity Fabric. CDNA 3 Matrix Cores triple FP16 and BF16 performance and provide 6.8 times the INT8 performance compared to MI250X GPUs. The product is suited for deployments ranging from individual servers to exascale supercomputers.

AMD's Instinct accelerator lineup referenced in the ROCm 7.13 release includes the MI350X, MI355X, MI325X, MI300X, and MI210X. AMD GPU Driver 31.30 additionally enables the MI350P GPU, expanding the Instinct hardware ecosystem. These accelerators are targeted at enterprise datacenter deployment.

AMD positions the Instinct MI300 accelerators for generative AI and large language model workloads. AMD also markets EPYC 9754 and 9734 processors for cloud native computing and EPYC 9004 with 3D V-Cache for high performance technical computing. These products serve cloud, hyperscale, and technical computing customer segments.

AMD's ROCm 7.13 AI software stack consists of ROCm Core 7.13, AMD GPU Driver 31.30, and AMD GPU Virtualization 9.0. The release introduces a modular packaging and installation model, ROCm-Extras packages starting with the ROCm Validation Suite (RVS), and streamlined profiling and visualization capabilities. ROCm 7.13 delivers optimized performance for generative AI and large language models across supported Instinct hardware.

AMD: ROCm 7.13 supports GPU passthrough on Instinct MI350X, MI355X, MI325X, MI300X, and MI210X accelerators on KVM with Ubuntu and RHEL host and guest environments. It also supports GPU passthrough for MI300X on VMware ESXi 8.0 Update 3. GPU passthrough dedicates an entire GPU to a single virtual machine to deliver bare-metal performance.

AMD collaborates with NAVER Cloud to advance AI infrastructure in Korea and with Upstage to advance sovereign AI infrastructure in Korea. These partnerships indicate AMD AI infrastructure is available through Korean cloud providers.
AMD and Celestica announced a collaboration to advance the next era of AI with the Helios rack-scale AI platform. This represents a rack-scale AI system offering involving AMD technology.

Broadcom co-designs custom AI accelerator chips, also called XPUs or ASICs, with hyperscale cloud providers, tailoring the hardware to each customer's specific workloads rather than offering a standardized general-purpose GPU roadmap.

Broadcom supplies Google with custom TPUs; Google's Ironwood TPU delivers 2x performance per watt versus Trillium, 6x more HBM, 4.5x HBM bandwidth, and more than 10x peak performance per chip and per pod versus TPU v5p.

Broadcom: OpenAI and Broadcom co-designed AI accelerators optimized for inference and networked through Broadcom's Ethernet stack; the systems include networking, memory and compute customized for OpenAI's workloads, with rack deployment planned starting late next year.

Broadcom secured over $10 billion of orders for AI racks based on XPUs from a fourth qualified hyperscale customer, and Broadcom states that three hyperscalers plus a fourth are each racing toward 1 million XPU clusters by the end of 2027.

Broadcom Thor Ultra is an 800G AI Ethernet NIC, described as the industry's first, capable of interconnecting hundreds of thousands of XPUs for trillion-parameter AI workloads; it is Ultra Ethernet Consortium compliant and supports 100G and 200G SerDes.
Broadcom 400G PCIe Gen 5.0 Ethernet adapters provide RoCE/RDMA connectivity with a third-generation RoCE pipeline, low-latency congestion control, and telemetry for AI data centers.
Broadcom Jericho4 fabric router supports congestion-free RoCE across data centers more than 100 kilometers apart to interconnect over one million XPUs.
Broadcom: Google deploys Broadcom-designed custom TPUs, with Broadcom's custom silicon relationship with Google reported as the most prominent hyperscale AI chip design partnership.
Broadcom: Meta is a Broadcom custom AI silicon customer.
Broadcom: ByteDance reportedly emerged as a third Broadcom custom silicon customer.

Broadcom: OpenAI partners with Broadcom to co-develop and deploy racks of OpenAI-designed AI accelerators and Ethernet network systems, with deployment planned starting in the second half of 2026 and completed by the end of 2029.
Intel Corp: Intel offers Intel® Gaudi® AI accelerators designed to bring compute advantages and choice to data center training and inference.
Intel Corp: Intel offers Intel® Data Center GPU Flex Series for virtual desktop infrastructure, media processing, and visual AI workloads.
Intel Corp: Intel offers Intel® Arc™ Pro Graphics for workstation performance, enabling users to run larger models and process richer data.
Intel Corp: Intel offers Intel® Data Center GPU Max Series, described as Intel's highest performing, highest density discrete GPU with up to 128 Intel® Xe Cores for HPC and AI acceleration.
Intel Corp: Intel offers Intel® Xeon® CPU Max processors with high-bandwidth memory for AI and supercomputing workloads.
Intel Corp: Intel Developer Cloud provides bare metal access to Intel® Data Center GPUs and Habana® Gaudi®2 accelerator systems for AI training and inference production workloads.

Intel Corp: Intel® oneAPI Deep Neural Network Library (oneDNN) provides optimized deep learning building blocks for CPUs and GPUs and is compatible with OpenVINO toolkit, AI Tools from Intel, PyTorch, and TensorFlow.
Intel Corp: Intel® oneAPI DL Framework Developer Toolkit includes oneDNN and oneCCL for building and optimizing deep learning frameworks, with support for Caffe, Theano, and Torch.
Intel Corp: Intel® oneAPI Toolkit supports development and optimization of PyTorch and TensorFlow for Intel CPUs and GPUs.
Intel Corp: Intel® Gaudi® AI accelerator supports PyTorch as the main framework for inference, with integration for Hugging Face models through the Optimum Habana library.
Intel Corp: IBM Cloud is the first cloud service provider to deploy Intel® Gaudi® 3 AI accelerators to customers.
Intel Corp: Intel® Gaudi® 3 instances on IBM Cloud are priced at approximately 30% less per hour than the GPU instances tested in the same environment.
Intel Corp: Intel® Gaudi® 3 demonstrated 92% more cost efficiency (performance per dollar) than competition on Meta's Llama-3.1-405B-Instruct-FP8 model with large context sizes.
Intel Corp: First-generation Intel® Gaudi® AI accelerator powers AWS DL1 instances delivering up to 40% better price/performance training compared to comparable GPU-based instances.
Intel Corp: Intel Developer Cloud offers access to AI accelerators with hourly rate pricing, cloud credits, and optional enterprise support and reserved pricing.
Intel Corp: Intel directs customers to authorized distributors, suppliers, and resellers for pricing and product availability information rather than publishing list prices directly.
Intel Corp: Intel offers Intel Gaudi Accelerators as data center AI accelerators for AI workloads. These accelerators are available through AWS DL1 accelerated compute instances.

The artificial intelligence (AI) data center graphics processing units (GPUs) market is projected to rise from $11.12 billion in 2025 to $32.3 billion by 2030, reflecting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 23.8%.
Intel cancelled its Falcon Shores GPU to pivot to Jaguar Shores, a rack-scale AI accelerator.
Crescent Island is a Xe3P-based inference-optimized data center GPU first announced on October 14, 2025 with 160GB of LPDDR5X and customer sampling expected in the second half of 2026.
Intel detailed it at Computex 2026 as a 350W air-cooled PCIe card supporting data types from FP4 through FP64. The announced card has 160GB.
North America dominated the gpu as a service market with a market share of 48.5% in 2025.

The global gpu as a service market size was valued at USD 8.2 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow from USD 10.26 billion in 2026 to USD 61.54 billion by 2034, registering a CAGR of 25.1% during the forecast period from 2026 to 2034.

Regional capital-expenditure outlays are on pace to claim a significant share of the global USD 527 billion hyperscaler budget in 2026 as cloud operators position Asia-Pacific as the world’s largest AI compute hub.
Japan’s Digital Agency, working with Fujitsu and Microsoft, committed JPY 1.6 trillion (USD 10.3 billion) in 2024 to build sovereign cloud zones.
China issued directives in 2025 mandating that government AI inference migrate to Ascend GPUs by 2027, guaranteeing thousands of annual domestic shipments.
Supermicro and #Verda 's deployment in Europe runs on the latest NVIDIA Blackwell Systems and is powered by 100% renewable energy.
SOOFI is building its foundation models using NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Nano and Super, as well as industrial AI cloud.
Alphabet’s Google Cloud unveiled a slew of new products and services at Google Cloud Next 2024.

even non-U.S. operators may face liability under the EAR if restricted GPUs controlled technology or sanctioned end users are present in their facilities
